questions.q: Why does Discovery require a MID Server, with no exception?
options: ServiceNow's cloud instance can't reach a customer's internal network directly; the MID Server is what actually sends probes onto the target range and relays results back
Discovery can run entirely from the cloud instance without any on-premises component
A MID Server is only an optional performance improvement for Discovery
MID Servers are only needed for REST integrations, never for Discovery
questions.explain: Course 7 established that the cloud instance has no direct access to an internal network — Discovery depends on the MID Server to bridge that gap.

questions.q: What does the network and firewall access requirement for Discovery actually mean?
options: The MID Server's location needs real, permitted access through any firewalls out to every IP address in the scanned range
Network access only matters for Horizontal Discovery, never Vertical Discovery
Firewalls must be fully disabled for Discovery to work at all
The ServiceNow cloud instance needs an inbound firewall port opened
questions.explain: If the MID Server can't route to the target subnet or a firewall blocks the needed ports, the scan won't find anything there.

questions.q: Why doesn't one Credential record cover every device type Discovery might scan?
options: Only Windows servers ever require a credential record
Discovery never actually needs to authenticate to any device
Credential records are universal and work identically across all protocols
Different device types use different protocols — SSH for Linux, WMI for Windows, SNMP for network devices — and credentials are protocol-specific
questions.explain: SSH and WMI credentials, for example, are not interchangeable — Discovery needs the matching credential for whatever protocol a device actually speaks.

questions.q: What happens when a MID Server has network access to a device but no matching credential for its protocol?
options: Discovery fails completely and detects nothing about the address at all
The lack of a credential has no effect on what Discovery collects
Discovery automatically creates full detail using a default credential
Discovery can usually detect something is listening but can't authenticate, so the resulting CI ends up thin with little detail
questions.explain: Without the right credential, Discovery can't authenticate to pull detailed information, producing a bare record rather than a fully detailed one.

questions.q: Which course's material does this lesson directly build on for both the MID Server and Credential requirements?
options: Course 2, which covered Service Mapping
Course 7, which covered what a MID Server does and course 7's Credential/authentication concepts
Chapter 1 of this course, which covered CMDB data quality
No earlier course material is relevant to this lesson
questions.explain: This lesson explicitly ties Discovery's requirements back to course 7's MID Server and credential/authentication material.
